 Just Seven Cars Sold, But Koenigsegg Still Has a Recall to Fix After One Rolled Away in Reverse
 By: 
 Saajan Jogia 
 Published: 
 October 30, 2026 - 1:00 pm 
 Saajan Jogia 
 October 30, 2026 
 Add MotorBiscuit as a preferred source 
 Swedish supercar maker Koenigsegg has recalled all 2025 and 2026 CC850 models due to an issue with the parking brake that can cause the vehicle to roll backward in reverse.
 According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) recall report , the unintended vehicle movement can increase the risk of a crash. The report, which identified seven CC850 units sold in the U.S., described the defect as follows:
 “When the EPB [electronic parking brake] is applied by pressing its button while the transmission is in Reverse and the engine is running, the EPB will not engage. No non-compliance with FMVSS 135 or UN R13-H identified; the condition is outside the scope of the static parking brake tests.”
 The report added:
 “If the driver leaves the vehicle in this state (with reverse gear engaged, engine running and no footbrake applied), the vehicle can roll if the car is on a non-flat surface without driver input. This increases the risk of unintended vehicle movement.”
 On October 12, 2026, Koenigsegg was notified of an incident involving a CC850 that rolled away after the driver attempted to engage the parking brake. The engine was running, reverse gear was selected, and the driver had exited the vehicle while it was parked on a slope. No injuries were reported. The automaker launched an internal investigation the same day, conducting real-world tests and assessing the likelihood of the issue occurring during normal vehicle use.
 After reviewing its findings on October 19, Koenigsegg concluded that a safety-related improvement was necessary and decided to issue a voluntary recall. The company confirmed that it had received no reports of injuries connected to the problem as of that date.
 The remedy for the problem will be to update the parking brake control software on all vehicles free of charge. The update will be delivered over the air (OTA) at no cost. In case a customer is unable to complete the software update, they can have the update installed at a Koenigsegg dealership.
 Koenigsegg began notifying its dealers on October 29, 2026, while owner notification letters are also scheduled to be mailed from that date. The software fix was expected to become available on October 22.
